package.title: 100 MDCAT Cell Biology MCQs with Answers and Explanations

questions.question: Which description best fits the fluid mosaic model of a cell membrane?
choices: A rigid layer of cellulose with embedded DNA
A phospholipid bilayer containing mobile proteins
A single protein sheet surrounding the cytoplasm
Two carbohydrate layers joined by ribosomes

questions.question: In a phospholipid bilayer, where do the hydrophilic heads normally face?
choices: Toward the watery environments inside and outside the cell
Toward the center of the bilayer only
Into the hydrophobic tails of neighboring lipids
Away from both the cytoplasm and extracellular fluid

questions.question: Which substance crosses a pure phospholipid bilayer most readily by simple diffusion?
What is the principal role of cholesterol in many animal cell membranes?
choices: It forms the cell's hereditary material
It helps moderate membrane fluidity and stability
It pumps glucose directly across the membrane

questions.question: A membrane protein that spans the entire phospholipid bilayer is called what?
Which membrane component commonly helps cells recognize one another?
choices: Carbohydrate chains attached to proteins or lipids
Free DNA strands in the bilayer
Cellulose fibers embedded in every animal membrane
Ribosomal RNA on the outer surface

questions.question: A membrane allows water through but blocks a particular solute. What property does this demonstrate?
A molecule moves from a region of higher concentration to lower concentration without a transport protein. What process is occurring?
Glucose moves down its concentration gradient through a carrier protein. Which process is this?
A cell uses ATP to move calcium ions against their concentration gradient. This is an example of what?
Which description defines osmosis?
choices: Net movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane
Movement of solute particles through a membrane protein
Engulfment of a particle by the cell membrane
Release of vesicle contents outside a cell

questions.question: A red blood cell is placed in a solution with a lower solute concentration than its cytoplasm. What is the likely result?
choices: Water enters the cell, which may swell
Water leaves the cell, which shrinks
The cell immediately forms a cell wall

questions.question: An animal cell is placed in a solution with a higher solute concentration than its cytoplasm. What is the expected effect?
choices: Water leaves the cell and it shrinks
Water enters the cell and it swells
The cell develops a large central vacuole
The solute concentration inside immediately becomes zero

questions.question: A plant cell placed in distilled water becomes firm rather than bursting. Which structure most directly limits excessive expansion?
What is the main function of the sodium-potassium pump in an animal cell?
choices: To move sodium and potassium ions across the membrane using energy
To copy DNA before cell division
To digest proteins in the cytoplasm
To move water through a channel without any ion movement

questions.question: A cell takes in a large particle by surrounding it with its plasma membrane. What is this process called?
A secretory vesicle fuses with the plasma membrane and releases its contents outside the cell. Which process is involved?
A white blood cell surrounds and internalizes a bacterium. Which form of endocytosis is this?
What is a typical function of an aquaporin?
choices: To provide a channel through which water can cross a membrane
To synthesize DNA in the nucleus
To attach amino acids to transfer RNA

questions.question: A substance crosses a membrane through a channel protein from high concentration to low concentration. Which statement is correct?
choices: The movement is facilitated diffusion and is down the gradient
The movement is active transport because a protein is involved
The movement is osmosis regardless of the substance
The movement must use ATP because it crosses a membrane

questions.question: Which organelle contains most of the genetic material in a typical eukaryotic cell?
Where are ribosomal subunits assembled in a eukaryotic cell?
What is the primary role of ribosomes?
Which organelle is especially associated with producing proteins for secretion from the cell?
Which function is commonly associated with smooth endoplasmic reticulum?
Which organelle modifies, sorts and packages many proteins received from the endoplasmic reticulum?
Which organelle contains digestive enzymes that break down material inside the cell?
Which organelle contains catalase, an enzyme that helps break down hydrogen peroxide?
In which organelle does most aerobic cellular respiration occur in a typical eukaryotic cell?
Which organelle captures light energy for photosynthesis in plant cells?
What is the main role of a large central vacuole in many plant cells?
Which cytoskeletal component forms the tracks used by cilia and many spindle structures?
Which cytoskeletal component is made mainly of actin and supports cell shape and movement?
What is one major function of the cytoskeleton?
choices: Supporting cell shape and helping move materials within the cell
Storing all hereditary information in every cell
Making the phospholipid bilayer impermeable to every molecule
Converting sunlight to chemical energy in animal cells

questions.question: Which structure is found in plant cells and commonly contains cellulose?
Which molecule is a major structural component of fungal cell walls?
Which substance is a major component of bacterial cell walls?
Which structure is the site of protein synthesis in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
What is the main function of the nuclear envelope?
choices: To enclose the nucleus and regulate exchange through nuclear pores
To synthesize ATP in the cytoplasm

questions.question: Which feature is characteristic of prokaryotic cells?
choices: Their DNA is enclosed in a nuclear envelope

questions.question: Where is the main chromosome located in a typical bacterial cell?
Which statement about a typical bacterial ribosome is correct?
choices: It is found only inside the nucleus

questions.question: Which structure is generally absent from prokaryotic cells?
Which structure is present in plant cells but absent from animal cells?
Which feature is common to both plant and animal cells?
choices: A large central vacuole in every cell

questions.question: Which organelle is found in eukaryotic cells but is absent from bacteria?
Which pair of organelles has its own DNA in eukaryotic cells?
A cell has a nucleus, mitochondria and a plasma membrane but no chloroplasts. Which conclusion is most defensible?
choices: It is eukaryotic, but these clues do not prove it is a plant cell
It must be a photosynthetic plant cell
It cannot carry out cellular respiration

questions.question: What is the main role of centrioles in many animal cells?
choices: Helping organize microtubules during cell division

questions.question: A typical motile eukaryotic cilium has which internal arrangement of microtubules?
choices: A single ring of nine actin filaments

questions.question: What is the function of the cell plate that forms during plant-cell cytokinesis?
choices: It develops into a partition between the daughter cells
It separates sister chromatids during anaphase

questions.question: A microscope has an eyepiece magnification of 10× and an objective magnification of 40×. What is the total magnification?
An image is 30 mm long when the actual specimen is 0.15 mm long. What is the magnification?
An object 0.02 mm long is viewed at 500× magnification. How long is its image?
What does resolution describe in microscopy?
choices: The ability to distinguish two nearby points as separate
The ability to make an image larger without limit
The brightness of the microscope lamp only

questions.question: All else being equal, which change can improve the resolving power of a light microscope?
choices: Using light of a shorter wavelength

questions.question: Which microscope is generally more suitable for viewing the three-dimensional surface detail of a specimen?
choices: Standard light microscope at low power

questions.question: Which microscope is generally used to examine internal ultrastructure in a thin specimen section?
Why are many biological specimens stained before viewing with a light microscope?
choices: To increase the specimen's actual size

questions.question: A microscope image measures 24 mm, and the specimen's actual length is 0.08 mm. What is the magnification?
A specimen is 0.5 mm long and viewed at 40× magnification. What is its image length?
What is a likely advantage of an electron microscope over a light microscope?
choices: It can resolve much smaller details
It always shows living cells in natural color
It uses visible light to form its image

questions.question: Why can a conventional light microscope not resolve structures much smaller than the wavelength of visible light?
choices: Diffraction limits the detail that can be distinguished
Visible light permanently destroys all small structures
The eyepiece converts every small structure into DNA

questions.question: During which part of the cell cycle is DNA replicated?
Which sequence gives the usual order of the main cell-cycle stages?
What is the main event of G1 phase?
choices: Cell growth and normal cellular activity

questions.question: What happens to DNA during S phase?
choices: It is translated into protein directly
It is divided equally between four cells

questions.question: What is a typical role of G2 phase?
choices: Preparing for cell division after DNA replication
Replicating the cell's DNA for the first time
Separating homologous chromosomes in meiosis I

questions.question: What is the usual outcome of mitosis followed by cytokinesis in a diploid body cell?
choices: Two daughter cells with the same chromosome number as the parent
Four cells with half the parent's chromosome number
One cell with twice the parent's chromosome number

questions.question: During which stage of mitosis do chromosomes line up near the cell's equator?
During which stage of mitosis do sister chromatids separate and move toward opposite poles?
What generally happens to the nuclear envelope during early mitosis in animal cells?
At the end of mitosis, what forms around each set of separated chromosomes?
choices: A second plasma membrane inside the nucleus

questions.question: How does cytokinesis differ in a typical animal cell and a typical plant cell?
choices: Animal cells form a cleavage furrow; plant cells form a cell plate
Animal cells form a cell plate; plant cells form a cleavage furrow
Only animal cells divide their cytoplasm
Only plant cells separate their chromosomes

questions.question: A diploid cell has 12 chromosomes before DNA replication. How many chromosomes does it have after S phase, before chromatids separate?
A human body cell has completed DNA replication but has not yet divided. How many chromosomes and chromatids does it contain?
What is the chromosome number in a normal human gamete?
What is the main purpose of meiosis in sexually reproducing organisms?
choices: To produce haploid cells for sexual reproduction
To make genetically identical body cells for growth
To double chromosome number in every generation
To repair every damaged cell membrane

questions.question: In which stage does crossing over normally occur?
What separates during anaphase I of meiosis?
choices: The two DNA strands of every gene

questions.question: What separates during anaphase II of meiosis?
choices: The cell wall from the plasma membrane
The two nuclei formed in meiosis I

questions.question: A diploid cell with 20 chromosomes completes meiosis. How many chromosomes will each normal haploid product have?
How many cells are typically produced from one cell after meiosis I and meiosis II are complete?
Which process usually produces daughter cells genetically most similar to the original body cell?
What is the main source of genetic variation created during prophase I of meiosis?
choices: Separation of sister chromatids in mitosis

questions.question: If a cell completes DNA replication but does not proceed through division, what has happened to its DNA amount compared with before S phase?
choices: It has been reduced by half
It has become four times greater

questions.question: A drug prevents spindle microtubules from attaching to chromosomes. Which event is most directly disrupted?
choices: Accurate movement and separation of chromosomes
Synthesis of phospholipids in smooth ER

questions.question: A cell has 8 chromosomes at the start of mitosis. After normal mitosis and cytokinesis, how many chromosomes are expected in each daughter cell?
A plant cell is placed in a concentrated salt solution and its membrane pulls away from the cell wall. What best explains this observation?
choices: Water left the cell by osmosis
Salt entered and dissolved the cell wall
The nucleus moved out through the cell wall
The cell made a new chloroplast

questions.question: A cell placed in an isotonic solution shows no net change in volume. Which statement best explains why?
choices: Water moves in both directions at equal rates
Solutes cannot move anywhere in the cell
The membrane has become completely impermeable

questions.question: A membrane pump transports a substance from lower concentration to higher concentration. Which condition is generally necessary?
choices: A concentration gradient pointing in the same direction
The absence of all membrane proteins
A cell wall made of cellulose

questions.question: A cell's membrane proteins are damaged, but its phospholipid bilayer remains intact. Which process is most likely to be impaired?
choices: Transport of many ions across the membrane
Diffusion of oxygen through the bilayer

questions.question: A secreted protein is being made by a cell. Which route best describes its usual path?
choices: Ribosome on rough ER, transport vesicle, Golgi apparatus, secretory vesicle

questions.question: A cell that produces large amounts of steroid hormones would be expected to have abundant what?
A cell that engulfs and digests many bacteria would especially rely on which organelle?
A cell's mitochondria are severely impaired. Which cellular process is most directly affected?
choices: DNA base pairing in the nucleus

questions.question: A mutation prevents a cell from producing functional ribosomes. Which process is directly impaired?
Which observation best indicates that a cell is actively dividing by mitosis?
choices: Condensed chromosomes attached to spindle fibers
A large number of dissolved sugars in the cytoplasm
Proteins being packaged in the Golgi apparatus

questions.question: A cell has 6 homologous pairs of chromosomes. How many chromosomes does it have in total?
A cell's chromosome number is 2n = 14. How many chromosomes are in a normal haploid cell from this organism?
